user_query: I need an image classification model for a furniture marketplace that categorizes the primary product in an uploaded photo as a chair, sofa, table, cabinet and or lamp. Please use the dinov2 vits14 and LoRA. The model will run on a CPU-only system with 8 GB of RAM.

model_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: User-required model override selected 'dinov2_vits14'. The user requires using DinoV2 with ViT-S14 backbone and LoRA for a CPU-only setup with 8 GB RAM. The dinov2_vits14 candidate directly satisfies this architectural and training constraint. LoRA enables training with a reduced parameter footprint, which is advantageous for CPU-only environments. The dataset provides five target classes (chair, sofa, table, cabinet, lamp) with substantial SOP-based training samples per class (roughly 3.4k–6.4k per class) and additional CIFAR100 samples that can offer diversity, though not domain-aligned with furniture. The requested low-latency, medium-accuracy trade-off on CPU is challenging for a large ViT, so plan to mitigate with lightweight configurations (e.g., small input resolution, restrained LoRA rank, backbone freezing, careful batch sizing). If latency or memory become prohibitive, consider alternative lighter backbones or reduced-resolution inputs as fallbacks.
uncertainties: CPU latency and memory footprint for DinoV2 ViT-S14 with LoRA on 8 GB RAM are not pre-measured here and require runtime profiling.
Exact LoRA configuration (rank, alpha) is not specified; final memory usage depends on these settings.
Domain shift between SOP-like product images and marketplace furniture images may affect real-world accuracy; additional domain-adaptive fine-tuning may be beneficial.
